builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: How Complete Must an Environment Be to Train a Capable GUI Agent?
summary: It replaces full-feature executable GUI training environments with MobileGym-Lite, which retains complete reward and data coverage while pruning application features that the tasks do not use. It costs environment-engineering effort to identify and remove unused features, and it reduces environment construction cost while training a 4B vision-language agent, which is feasible on a single 24 GB GPU. It can fail because the reported improvement is sensitive to episode weighting: the gain reverses under equal per-episode weighting and vanishes when pruned-task episodes are balanced, and single-reference-path verifiers degrade success by over ten points.
rationale: If the reader builds RL training environments for GUI agents, keeping reward and data coverage complete while pruning unused features is a validated, low-cost design rule, but the headline gain depends on task-weighting effects that require validation on their own task mix.

claims.statement: It replaces full-feature executable GUI training environments with MobileGym-Lite, which retains complete reward and data coverage while pruning application features that the tasks do not use. It costs environment-engineering effort to identify and remove unused features, and it reduces environment construction cost while training a 4B vision-language agent, which is feasible on a single 24 GB GPU. It can fail because the reported improvement is sensitive to episode weighting: the gain reverses under equal per-episode weighting and vanishes when pruned-task episodes are balanced, and single-reference-path verifiers degrade success by over ten points.

MobileGym-Lite reaches 55.48% success versus 51.61% for the full environment when training Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct; pruning unneeded features alone raises success to 56.13%, while single-path reward verification lowers success by 10.53 points.
